existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `InsurancePlan` has substantial local breaking changes: R4 product-level fields moved to `InsuranceProduct`, repeatable `plan` entries became separate root-level plan resources, and `identifier`/`type` are not safe to map by path alone. The largest uncertainty is the absence of official conversion maps and terminology expansions.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should split each R4 `InsurancePlan` into product and plan resources, preserve modifier `status` on `InsuranceProduct`, explode multiple R4 `plan` entries into multiple R6 `InsurancePlan` resources, and apply source-path-aware rules for identifiers and type. Down-conversion from R6 requires dereferencing `InsurancePlan.product` or accepting loss/extension-based representation.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural element, cardinality, flag, and local constraint changes because both primary StructureDefinitions are present and the R6 `InsuranceProduct` counterpart is available locally. Confidence is lower for exact terminology code deltas and rationale because official diffs, narrative pages, and live terminology expansions were not provided.

rationaleMd:
InsurancePlan keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 4 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 1 potential hard break(s), 3 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 52/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

6 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with more than one root `type` exceed R6 max 1; semantic/documentation: a single R4 product type copied to R6 `InsurancePlan.type` can be valid but wrong.

topFindings.title: InsurancePlan was split from a combined product/plan resource into a plan resource backed by InsuranceProduct

topFindings.title: InsurancePlan.identifier kept the path but changed from product identifier to plan/group identifier semantics
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: no old-valid/new-invalid instance break is guaranteed, but path-based migration can produce valid R6 resources whose identifiers refer to the wrong business object; runtime/API/search behavior can then match the wrong plan or product.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: an R6 product reference has no native R4 field and must be inlined, dereferenced, extended, or dropped; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism for this optional addition.
